v_age_group = doc.add_variable(name="age_group", question=q_age)
v_age_group.set_coded(cl_age_group)
v_age_group.source_variable_references = [v_age.to_reference()]

v_emp_code = doc.add_variable(name="employment_status_code", question=q_employed)
v_emp_code.source_variable_references = [v_employed.to_reference()]

v_health_score = doc.add_variable(name="health_score", question=q_health)
v_health_score.source_variable_references = [v_health.to_reference()]

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

Exercise 5

v_master_ag = doc.add_variable(name="age_group_master", question=q_age)
v_master_ag.source_variable_references = [v_age_group.to_reference()]

v_master_emp = doc.add_variable(name="employment_status_master", question=q_employed)
v_master_emp.source_variable_references = [v_emp_code.to_reference()]

v_master_hs = doc.add_variable(name="health_score_master", question=q_health)
v_master_hs.source_variable_references = [v_health_score.to_reference()]

print(f"Variables: {len(doc.variables)}")

for v in doc.variables:
    sources = len(v.source_variable_references)
    if sources > 0:
        print(f"  {v.names[0].text}: {sources} source(s)")

Exercise 6

v_height = doc.add_variable(name="height_cm")
v_weight = doc.add_variable(name="weight_kg")

v_bmi = doc.add_variable(name="bmi")
v_bmi.source_variable_references = [
    v_height.to_reference(),
    v_weight.to_reference(),
]

print(f"BMI sources: {len(v_bmi.source_variable_references)}")

Exercise 7

current = v_master_hs
print(current.names[0].text)
while current.source_variable_references:
    current = doc.find(current.source_variable_references[0].identifier)
    print(current.names[0].text)

question = doc.find(current.question_references[0].identifier)
print(question.question_texts[0].text)

The loop stops at health_rating, the collection variable. Only its question link is left to follow.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which file is this?

D. The master file keeps only the final derived variables, ready for dissemination. The production file would also hold age, gender and employed.

Question 2 (O2): Which call fits this variable?

A. The values are whole numbers you can add and average, so the representation is numeric, with the valid range. A code list of 366 categories would hide that, and text would allow "three" or "a few".

Question 3 (O3): How do you record that smoker came from q_smoke?

B. The question= parameter adds the link to question_references. source_variable_references is for source variables, not questions.

Question 4 (O4): A BMI variable is computed from height and weight. How many source_variable_references does it have?

C. BMI has 2 source variable references, one for height and one for weight, because it is derived from both.

Question 5 (O4): What does source_variable_references track?

B. source_variable_references is a list of references pointing to the variables that were used to compute a derived variable. Questions go in question_references, and the code list in the representation.

Question 6 (O5): What does this code print?

A. The loop follows health_score_master → health_score → health_rating, and stops there because health_rating has no source variable. It prints a variable name; the question text needs one more step through question_references.

docs.title: Module 12: Data linkage: combining records across datasets
Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 1

A sample answer: "Linkage combines records from the two files that describe the same person, using a variable they share. The register already holds every hospital visit, so linking gives us that information without asking respondents anything new, which reduces their burden. The counts also come from records rather than from memory, and the linked file can answer questions neither file answers alone, such as whether people who rate their health as poor visit hospital more often."

Exercise 2

  • (a) Deterministic: both files carry the same reliable ID, so an exact match on it is enough.
  • (b) Probabilistic: there is no shared ID, and the names have errors, so you weigh agreement across several quasi-identifiers and apply a threshold.
  • (c) Deterministic: the respondent ID is stable across waves.

Exercise 3

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(
    title="Canadian Community Health Survey 2021",
    agency="statcan.gc.ca",
)
q_key = doc.add_question(text="Anonymized linkage key")
q_health = doc.add_question(text="How would you rate your general health?")
survey_key = doc.add_variable(name="anon_id", question=q_key)
survey_health = doc.add_variable(name="health_rating", question=q_health)

admin = doc.add_study(title="Hospital Admissions Register 2021")
admin_ds = doc.study(admin.identifier)
admin_key = admin_ds.add_variable(name="anon_id")
admin_visits = admin_ds.add_variable(name="hospital_visits")

print(f"Survey variables: {len(doc.variables)}")
print(f"hospital_visits found: {doc.find(admin_visits.identifier) is not None}")

doc.variables counts only the survey's two variables. The register's variables are in the second study, and doc.find() still reaches them.

Exercise 4

survey_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")
admin_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")

print(f"Survey anon_id: {survey_key.get_property('linkage_role')}")
print(f"Register anon_id: {admin_key.get_property('linkage_role')}")
print(f"health_rating: {survey_health.get_property('linkage_role')}")

health_rating was never tagged, so get_property() returns None.

Exercise 5

cmp = doc.add_comparison(name="Survey-to-Admin Microdata Linkage 2021")
key_match = cmp.correspondence(
    commonality="Anonymized personal identifier common to both sources.",
    weight=1.0,
)
cmp.add_variable_map(
    survey_key.to_reference(),
    admin_key.to_reference(),
    correspondence=key_match,
)
cmp.set_property("linkage_method", "deterministic")
cmp.set_property("match_rate", "0.94")

print(f"Comparisons: {len(doc.comparisons)}")
print(f"Variable maps: {len(cmp.variable_maps)}")
method = cmp.get_property("linkage_method")
print(f"{method}, match rate {cmp.get_property('match_rate')}")

Exercise 6

linked = doc.add_variable(name="health_by_hospital_use")
linked.source_variable_references = [
    survey_health.to_reference(),
    admin_visits.to_reference(),
]

print(f"Linked variable sources: {len(linked.source_variable_references)}")

Exercise 7

prob = doc.add_comparison(name="Probabilistic Linkage")
prob.set_property("linkage_method", "probabilistic")
partial = prob.correspondence(
    commonality="Agreement across date of birth, sex, and postal code.",
    weight=0.85,
)

for name in ("date_of_birth", "sex", "postal_code"):
    survey_var = doc.add_variable(name=name)
    register_var = admin_ds.add_variable(name=name)
    survey_var.set_property("linkage_role", "matching")
    register_var.set_property("linkage_role", "matching")
    prob.add_variable_map(
        survey_var.to_reference(),
        register_var.to_reference(),
        correspondence=partial,
    )

print(f"Variable maps: {len(prob.variable_maps)}")
print(prob.get_property("linkage_method"))

A weight below 1.0 records that agreement on these fields is strong evidence of a match, but not proof.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O1): Why link instead of asking a new question?

A. Linkage combines records about the same person from existing files. It reduces respondent burden and creates information that neither file holds alone. It still needs a common variable to join the records.

Question 2 (O2): Which linkage method fits these files?

B. With no reliable key and errors in some fields, an exact match on one field would miss true pairs (name typos) or join the wrong people (many share a postal code). Probabilistic linkage combines the evidence from several quasi-identifiers.

Question 3 (O3): How do you add a variable to the register study?

C. doc.study() returns a cursor for that study, and its add_* methods add items there. doc.add_variable() always adds to the primary study, the survey.

Question 4 (O4): What does this code print?

D. Only survey_key was tagged. get_property() returns the value stored under the key, or None when the item has no such key.

Question 5 (O5): Which call records that the two keys correspond exactly?

A. A variable map in the Comparison records that the survey key corresponds to the register key, and the correspondence weight 1.0 says they are the same identifier. Option B tags one side only; option C records a quality figure; option D records provenance.

Question 6 (O6): How do you record that a linked variable draws on two source files?

B. source_variable_references holds a Reference to each source variable (here, one to the survey variable and one to the admin variable), even though they live in different studies.

docs.title: Module 13: Custom properties, find, remove, and validate
Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="research.org")
q_age = doc.add_question(text="How old are you?")
q_income = doc.add_question(text="What is your household income?")
q_name = doc.add_question(text="What is your full name?")

q_income.set_property("sensitivity", "high")
q_name.set_property("sensitivity", "high")
q_name.set_property("data_source", "self-reported")
print(q_name.properties)
# -> {'sensitivity': 'high', 'data_source': 'self-reported'}

print(q_name.remove_property("data_source"))  # -> True
print(q_name.properties)  # -> {'sensitivity': 'high'}

Exercise 2

v_age = doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q_age)

found = doc.find(v_age.identifier)
print(f"Found: {found.names[0].text}")  # -> Found: Age
print(doc.find("not-an-identifier"))  # -> None

doc.find() returns None when nothing matches; it does not raise an error.

Exercise 3

doc.remove(q_name.identifier)
print(f"Questions: {len(doc.questions)}")  # -> Questions: 2
print(doc.remove(q_name.identifier))  # -> False

The second call finds nothing to remove, so it returns False.

Exercise 4

doc.remove(q_age.identifier)

for finding in doc.lint():
    if finding.severity == "error":
        print(finding.rule_id)  # -> ddi.reference.integrity

v_age.question_references = [
    ref for ref in v_age.question_references if ref.identifier != q_age.identifier
]
errors = [finding for finding in doc.lint() if finding.severity == "error"]
print(f"Lint errors: {len(errors)}")  # -> Lint errors: 0

Removing the Age variable too (doc.remove(v_age.identifier)) is also a correct fix, if the variable means nothing without its question.

Exercise 5

issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")  # -> Issues: 1
print(issues[0].context)  # -> <r:Version> 1.a

# A version is numbers separated by dots
q_income.version = "1.1"
issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")
print(issues[0].context)  # -> <d:Text> Revenu du ménage ?

# A language tag uses a hyphen, not an underscore
q_income.question_texts[-1].lang = "fr-CA"
issues = doc.validate()
print(f"Issues: {len(issues)}")  # -> Issues: 0

doc.save("household-clean.xml")

The first run reports only the version. The language tag shows up once the version is fixed, which is why you validate again after every fix.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O1): What does print(q.properties) show after these two calls?

C. Setting a key the item already has replaces its value. An item has at most one value per key.

Question 2 (O1): Which line removes the property data_source from the item q?

A. remove_property() removes the key and returns True. B deletes the key from a new dictionary that properties built, so the item keeps it. C removes items by identifier, not properties. D only reads the value.

Question 3 (O2): doc.remove(v.identifier) just returned True. What does doc.find(v.identifier) return now?

D. The variable is no longer in the document, so nothing matches, and doc.find() returns None rather than raising an error.

Question 4 (O3): You remove a question that a variable refers to. doc.validate() returns an empty list. Is the document ready to share?

B. Validation checks the shape of the file against the schema, not whether each reference finds its target. Lint does. doc.save() warns about the broken reference but keeps it.

Question 5 (O4): Validation reports this issue. Which fix is right?

A. The message says the xml:lang value en_US does not match the allowed pattern, which uses hyphens. The context shows which text holds it. Removing the question (B) loses data to hide the problem; C and D do not change the tag.

Question 6 (O4): Validation reports this issue on a question's version. Which value passes?

C. The pattern allows numbers separated by dots, and nothing else. Validate again after the fix to confirm it, and to see any issue the first one hid.

docs.title: Module 14: Custom fields: extend the standard for your organization
Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="survey.example.org")
q_income = doc.add_question(text="What is your household income?")
income = doc.add_variable(name="income", question=q_income)

study = doc.study_unit
study.set_property("myorg:retention_policy", "destroy after 7 years")
study.set_property("myorg:security_class", "Confidential")
income.set_property("myorg:source_system", "CRM-2024")

print(study.properties)
print(income.get_property("myorg:source_system"))  # -> CRM-2024

The retention policy and the classification describe the whole dataset, so they go on the study. The source system describes one variable.

Exercise 2

from ddi_l.models.base import UserID

income.user_ids.append(UserID(value="CAT-000734", type_of_user_id="InternalCatalogue"))

uid = income.user_ids[0]
print(f"{uid.type_of_user_id}: {uid.value}")  # -> InternalCatalogue: CAT-000734

(a) UserID: another system can look the variable up by this number, so it identifies the item. (b) and (c) are custom properties: they describe the item.

Exercise 3

from uuid import uuid4

from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem

# Build the controlled vocabulary. Each allowed value needs a Category (its
# meaning) AND a Code in the list that references it; a Category alone is not
# in any list. Each Code gets its own UUID4-based URN.
quality_codes = doc.add_code_list(name="Quality Flag Codes")
for value in ("validated", "provisional", "suppressed"):
    category = doc.add_item(Category, name=value)
    quality_codes.codes.append(
        CodeItem(
            agency=quality_codes.agency,
            identifier=str(uuid4()),
            version=quality_codes.version,
            value=value,
            category=category.to_reference(),
        )
    )

# A field whose value is drawn from the vocabulary, plus a field that
# references the code list defining the allowed values
income.set_property("myorg:quality_flag", "validated")
income.set_property("myorg:quality_flag_codes", quality_codes)

print(income.get_property("myorg:quality_flag"))  # -> validated
print(income.get_property("myorg:quality_flag_codes").startswith("urn:ddi:"))

Objects stay attached

Variables you hold remain the objects the document serializes, before and after save().

Exercise 4

CUSTOM_FIELDS = {
    "myorg:source_system": "The system the data was extracted from.",
    "myorg:quality_flag": "Data-quality status (see Quality Flag Codes).",
    "myorg:steward": "The team accountable for the item.",
}


def set_catalog_field(item, key, value):
    if key not in CUSTOM_FIELDS:
        raise ValueError(f"{key!r} is not in the custom-field catalog")
    item.set_property(key, value)


set_catalog_field(income, "myorg:steward", "Survey Methods")
print(income.get_property("myorg:steward"))  # -> Survey Methods

try:
    set_catalog_field(income, "myorg:stewart", "Survey Methods")
except ValueError as error:
    print(f"Refused: {error}")
# -> Refused: 'myorg:stewart' is not in the custom-field catalog

Without the guard, the typo would create a second, misspelt field that no audit or reader looks for.

Exercise 5

q_income.set_property("myorg:steward", "Survey Methods")


def items_with_custom_fields(doc, prefix="myorg:"):
    count = 0
    for collection in (doc.questions, doc.variables):
        for item in collection:
            if any(key.startswith(prefix) for key in item.properties):
                count += 1
    return count


print(f"Items with custom fields: {items_with_custom_fields(doc)}")
# -> Items with custom fields: 2

The audit counts items, not fields: the income variable carries several myorg: fields and counts once.

Exercise 6

from pathlib import Path

doc.save("household-survey.xml")

reopened = ddi.open_ddi("household-survey.xml")
print(reopened.variables[0].get_property("myorg:source_system"))  # -> CRM-2024

xml = Path("household-survey.xml").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
print("<r:AttributeKey>myorg:source_system</r:AttributeKey>" in xml)  # -> True

The key sits in an r:AttributeKey, inside the r:UserAttributePair that also holds its r:AttributeValue.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O1): Which call records that the whole dataset is classified Confidential?

B. A fact about the whole dataset goes on the study, doc.study_unit. A and C put it on one item (and C drops the namespace prefix). D creates a variable, not a field.

Question 2 (O6): You save a document and search the XML for your key myorg:source_system. Where do you find it?

C. set_property writes an r:UserAttributePair with an r:AttributeKey and an r:AttributeValue, the standard's extension point for custom fields. That is why the field survives save and reopen.

Question 3 (O2): RM-2291 is the records-management system's number for a variable. Where do you record it?

A. The value identifies the variable in another system, so it is a UserID. Use a custom property when the value describes the item.

Question 4 (O3): quality_codes is a code list. What does get_property return after this call?

D. Passing a DDI item as the value stores its URN, a stable link to the code list. Properties always hold strings.

Question 5 (O4): With the catalog guard of section 8, what does set_catalog_field(income, 'myorg:stewart', 'X') do?

D. The key is not in CUSTOM_FIELDS, so the function raises before it calls set_property. The typo is caught instead of creating a misspelt field.

Question 6 (O5): A question has no properties; variable v1 has myorg:a and myorg:b; variable v2 has other:flag. What does items_with_custom_fields(doc) return?

A. Only v1 has a key that starts with myorg:. The audit counts items, not fields, so its two fields count once, and other:flag does not match the prefix.

docs.title: Module 15: Update and version your documents
Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 1

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Labour Force Survey v1", agency="stats.example.org")
q1 = doc.add_question(text="What is your current employment status?")
q1.question_texts.append(
    InternationalString(
        text="Quelle est votre situation d'emploi actuelle ?", lang="fr"
    )
)
q2 = doc.add_question(text="How many hours do you work per week?")
q3 = doc.add_question(text="Do you use a fax machine at work?")
doc.add_variable(name="EMPSTAT", label="Employment status", question=q1)

doc.save("survey-v1.xml")
print(f"Saved with {len(doc.questions)} questions and {len(doc.variables)} variable.")

Exercise 2

doc = ddi.open_ddi("survey-v1.xml")
print(f"Before: {len(doc.questions)} questions")

# Add a new question
doc.add_question(text="How many hours do you sleep per night?")

# Remove the outdated fax question
fax_q = next(
    q
    for q in doc.questions
    if q.question_texts[0].text == "Do you use a fax machine at work?"
)
doc.remove(fax_q.identifier)
print(f"After: {len(doc.questions)} questions")
print(doc.validate())  # -> []

The count is the same, but the content is not: one question in, one out. survey-v1.xml on disk is unchanged until you save over it, which you will not do.

Exercise 3

(a) Sub-version: 1.2.1. (b) Minor: 1.3.0. (c) Major: 2.0.0.

check = ddi.new_study(title="Version check", agency="example.org").study_unit

check.version = "1.2.0"
check.increment_minor_version()
print(check.version)  # -> 1.3.0

check.version = "1.2.0"
check.increment_major_version()
print(check.version)  # -> 2.0.0

Each increment resets the numbers to its right to zero.

Exercise 4

from ddi_l.models.base import VersionRationale

study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Added sleep question; retired fax question")
        ]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Survey Design Team"

errors = doc.validate()
if errors:
    print("Errors:", errors)
else:
    doc.save("survey-v2.xml")
    print(f"Version: {study.version}")  # -> Version: 1.1
    for r in study.version_rationales:
        for d in r.descriptions:
            print(f"Rationale: {d.text}")
    print(f"Responsibility: {study.version_responsibility}")

Exercise 5

doc = ddi.open_ddi("survey-v2.xml")

status_q = next(
    q
    for q in doc.questions
    if q.question_texts[0].text == "What is your current employment status?"
)
for text in status_q.question_texts:
    if text.lang == "en":
        text.text = "What was your main activity last week?"
    if text.lang == "fr":
        text.text = "Quelle était votre activité principale la semaine dernière ?"

status_q.increment_subversion(allow_dotted=True)
status_q.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Aligned wording with the ILO definition")
        ]
    )
)

# Repoint the variable that references the question
for variable in doc.variables:
    variable.question_references = [
        status_q.to_reference() if ref.identifier == status_q.identifier else ref
        for ref in variable.question_references
    ]

print(f"{status_q.question_texts[0].text} (version {status_q.version})")
# -> What was your main activity last week? (version 1.0.1)
print(status_q.question_texts[1].text)

errors = [finding for finding in doc.lint() if finding.severity == "error"]
print(f"Lint errors: {len(errors)}")  # -> Lint errors: 0
doc.save("survey-v3.xml")

Skip the repointing loop once and run doc.lint(): it reports a ddi.reference.integrity error for EMPSTAT.

Exercise 6

three_way = doc.add_code_list(name="Status (3)", label="Status (3)")
add_codes(
    doc,
    three_way,
    [("1", "Employed"), ("2", "Unemployed"), ("3", "Not in labour force")],
)
four_way = doc.add_code_list(name="Status (4)", label="Status (4)")
add_codes(
    doc,
    four_way,
    [("1", "Employed"), ("2", "Unemployed"), ("3", "Student"), ("4", "Retired")],
)

empstat = next(v for v in doc.variables if v.names[0].text == "EMPSTAT")
empstat.set_coded(three_way)

# The switch
empstat.set_coded(four_way)
empstat.increment_major_version()
empstat.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(
                text="Split 'Not in labour force' into Student and Retired"
            )
        ]
    )
)

reference = empstat.variable_representation.code_representation.code_list_reference
print(doc.find(reference.identifier).names[0].text)  # -> Status (4)
print(empstat.version)  # -> 2

A major bump fits: last year's code 3 no longer means the same thing.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O1): You opened survey-2023.xml and added two questions. Which line keeps last year's file unchanged?

C. Saving under a new name writes the update to a new file and leaves survey-2023.xml as it was. A overwrites last year's file. B checks but saves nothing; D reads a file that does not exist yet.

Question 2 (O2): A question is at version 1.2.3. You call increment_minor_version(). What is its version now?

D. The minor number goes up by one, and the number to its right resets to zero.

Question 3 (O2): A variable is at version 1. You call increment_subversion() with no arguments. What happens?

A. An item keeps the numbering it has. A one-part version stays one-part unless you pass allow_dotted=True, because some tools only read whole-number versions.

Question 4 (O3): Which code records why question q changed and who changed it?

B. A VersionRationale holds the reason, and version_responsibility names who made the change. A changes the label; C stores a custom field that no DDI tool reads as a rationale.

Question 5 (O4): You reworded a question and bumped its version. doc.lint() now reports ddi.reference.integrity. What do you fix?

C. A DDI reference names one exact version. After the bump, the variable's question_references still name the old one, so replace them with question.to_reference(). doc.validate() does not check references, which is why D is wrong.

Question 6 (O5): How do you switch a variable from one code list to another?

A. set_coded() replaces the variable's representation with one that references the new code list. Then bump the variable's version, record a rationale, and remove the old code list if nothing else uses it.

Question 7 (O5): A variable's answers change from Yes/No to Every day, Some days, Never. Which increment fits?

D. New answer categories change what the variable holds. When answers are no longer comparable, the change is major.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
Exercise 1

Q5 is PetAge > 10. Q6 shows when Q5 does not, including a missing age, so it is not PetAge > 10 (or, saying the same out loud, PetAge <= 10 or missing(PetAge); pick one form and keep it).

print(normal("PetAge > 10"))  # -> PetAge > 10
print(normal("not PetAge > 10"))  # -> not PetAge > 10

Had Q6 been PetAge <= 10, a respondent with no age would see neither Q5 nor Q6.

The edit fires for 35 only. For 12 the comparison is false, and for a missing age a comparison is always false. To flag a missing age, you would write a second edit with when: missing(PetAge).

Exercise 2

(a) The jump fires only on "No". A respondent who did not answer H1 does not jump, so sees H2 and H3: the gate is not Own = 2. (b) Owners only: Own = 1. The two differ only when H1 has no answer, so write the one the survey means. H4 has no gate: everyone sees it.

print(normal("not Own = 2"))  # -> not Own = 2
print(normal("Own = 1"))  # -> Own = 1

Exercise 3

The pet kind comes from a closed list, so it is a code: the question PetKind itself, with the code list Species, whose labels are in English and French. Q3's English text pipes in PetKind, and so does its French text; each shows the label of its language (check once that your tool's piped text shows labels). No derived variable is needed, since the answer already is the value.

code_lists:
  Species:
    values:
      1: {en: Dog, fr: Chien}
      2: {en: Cat, fr: Chat}
      3: {en: Bird, fr: Oiseau}

Exercise 4

spec: my-pets
version: "1"
languages: [en, fr]

code_lists:
  Species:
    values:
      1: {en: Dog, fr: Chien}
      2: {en: Cat, fr: Chat}
      3: {en: Bird, fr: Oiseau}

modules:
  - id: household
    questions:
      - id: PetCount
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 20, decimals: 0}}

  - id: pets
    gate: PetCount > 0
    questions:
      - id: PetKind
        domain: {code: {list: Species}}
      - id: PetName
        domain: {text: {max_length: 50}}
        gate: answered(PetKind)
      - id: PetAge
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 40, decimals: 0}}
      - id: VetVisits
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 50, decimals: 0}}
        gate: PetAge > 10
      - id: Toys
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 99, decimals: 0}}
        gate: not PetAge > 10

  - id: visits
    questions:
      - id: LastVisit
        domain: {date: {type: Date}}

edits:
  - id: age_over_30
    when: PetAge > 30
    module: pets
    message:
      en: Is the pet really over 30?
      fr: L’animal a-t-il vraiment plus de 30 ans ?
    severity: warning

"If 0, go to Section 3" becomes the gate of the module it skips, pets. If ddi spec validate reports a problem, its path says where: modules[1].questions[2] is the third question of the second module.

Exercise 5

Finding Wrong What to change spec.gate.missing (module pets) instrument Show pets only when PetCount > 0: wrap it in an IfThenElse with that condition. spec.domain.type (PetKind, PetName, PetAge) instrument The draft's questions have no response domain. Give PetKind the Species codes, PetName text up to 50 characters, PetAge a number from 0 to 40. spec.gate.unverifiable (PetName) neither Check by hand: the draft's condition reads answered(PetKind), the spec's gate. Nothing to change. spec.language.missing (PetAge) instrument Add the French text of the question. spec.item.extra (PetColour) spec It was added on purpose: add PetColour and its domain to the pets module of the spec, and give the spec a new version. spec.edit.unverifiable (age_range) neither Not compared. Check the edit in the instrument by hand.

Items with a new version after the two fixes: PetAge's question (new text); the PetAge construct, which refers to it; the pets sequence, which refers to the construct; the new IfThenElse for the module gate, at its first version; the main sequence, which now refers to that IfThenElse instead of to pets; and the instrument. The household sequence, the other questions and constructs, and Ask PetName keep their versions. All new and revised items share one versionDate and one responsibility.

Exercise 6

The scenario says Q6 shows when Q5 does not, so a missing age must show Q6: the spec (not PetAge > 10) is right. Change the instrument's gate. The two gates differ only for a missing age, which is why equivalent() and ddi conform treat them as different.

docs.title: Quiz
docs.text:
Question 1 (O2): PetAge has no answer. Which gate is true?

C. A comparison is false without an answer, so A, B and D are false, and not turns A's false into true.

Question 2 (O2): An edit check has when: PetAge > 30. A respondent skips PetAge. Does the check fire?

B. The check fires when when is true, and PetAge > 30 is false when there is no answer.

Question 3 (O3): The document says: if Q4 > 10 ask Q5, otherwise Q6. A respondent with no age must see Q6. Which gate do you write for Q6?

D. not PetAge > 10 is true when PetAge > 10 is false, including when the age is missing. A and C are false on a missing age (and C also hides Q6 from a pet aged exactly 10). A second gate reads the same in every tool, which an else branch does not.

Question 4 (O4): Why does a month need no language-specific copies of its variable?

A. One code, two labels, one variable.

Question 5 (O1): ddi spec validate prints this. What do you fix?

B. Positions count from 0, so modules[0].questions[1] is the second question of the first module, and its numeric min is above its max. ddi spec validate reports problems, not warnings: the spec does not load until you fix it.

Question 6 (O5): ddi conform reports 0 errors and 12 warnings. Is the instrument right?

D. Read the warnings: a shared module that another spec covers is a typical one, and an unverifiable gate needs a check by hand. To be sure the check is live, change one gate in a copy of the spec and expect exactly one new error.

Question 7 (O5): ddi conform reports spec.item.extra for PetColour, which the survey owner added on purpose. What do you change?

C. Here the spec is the one that is wrong: it does not list a question the survey needs. Fix the record, version it, and run the check again.

Question 8 (O5): You fix the condition of the IfThenElse that gates PetName, inside the pets sequence. Which items get a new version?

A. The changed item and every item that refers to it, up to the instrument. Items that refer to nothing you changed, such as the household sequence, keep their versions.

docs.title: Module 17: Real-world capstone projects
docs.text:
Track A: University Student: Document Your Thesis Dataset: Sample solution

One complete script for all the steps above, using thesis-data.csv.

import csv
from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem


def add_codes(doc, code_list, labels):
    """Add one Category and one Code per label, numbered from 1."""
    for number, label in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        category = doc.add_item(Category, name=label, label=label)
        code_list.codes.append(
            CodeItem(
                agency=code_list.agency,
                identifier=str(uuid4()),
                version=code_list.version,
                value=str(number),
                category=category.to_reference(),
            )
        )


with open("thesis-data.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
columns = list(rows[0])

# Version 1.0
doc = ddi.new_study(title="Student Stress Survey 2024", agency="university.example.org")
# How each column was asked. StudentID is assigned and AnxietyScore is computed
# from a questionnaire, so neither gets a question of its own.
QUESTIONS = {
    "Age": "How old are you?",
    "Gender": "What is your gender?",
    "YearOfStudy": "What year of your program are you in?",
    "Program": "Which program are you enrolled in?",
    "StudyHours": "On a typical day, how many hours do you study?",
    "SleepHours": "On a typical night, how many hours do you sleep?",
    "WorkHours": "How many hours a week do you work for pay?",
    "ExerciseDays": "On how many days last week did you exercise?",
    "StressLevel": "On a scale of 1 to 10, how stressed have you felt this term?",
    "SoughtSupport": "Have you sought support from campus services this term?",
}
questions = {col: doc.add_question(text=text) for col, text in QUESTIONS.items()}
variables = {
    col: doc.add_variable(name=col, question=questions.get(col)) for col in columns
}

# One code list per coded column, from the values in the file
for col in ("Gender", "Program", "SoughtSupport"):
    code_list = doc.add_code_list(name=f"{col} Codes")
    add_codes(doc, code_list, sorted({row[col] for row in rows}))
    variables[col].set_coded(code_list)

doc.add_concept(name="Demographics")
doc.add_concept(name="Academic Workload")
doc.add_concept(name="Well-Being")
doc.add_universe(name="Undergraduate students aged 18-25")
variables["StudyHours"].set_property("dataSource", "Online survey tool")
variables["AnxietyScore"].set_property(
    "scoring", "Sum of a standard 10-item anxiety scale"
)

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
doc.save("thesis-v1.xml")

# Version 1.1: a derived variable and its lineage
doc = ddi.open_ddi("thesis-v1.xml")
by_name = {v.names[0].text: v for v in doc.variables}
stress_index = doc.add_variable(name="StressIndex")
stress_index.source_variable_references = [
    by_name["StressLevel"].to_reference(),
    by_name["AnxietyScore"].to_reference(),
]

study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[
            InternationalString(text="Added the derived StressIndex variable")
        ]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Thesis Author"

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v1.1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
# -> v1.1: 0 validation errors, 0 lint errors
doc.save("thesis-v1.1.xml")

Track B: Researcher: Package a Health Survey for Publication: Sample solution

One complete script, using health-survey.csv. Run ddi to-json health-survey-v1.xml --indent 2 > health-survey-v1.json after it.

import csv
from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem


def add_codes(doc, code_list, labels):
    """Add one Category and one Code per label, numbered from 1."""
    for number, label in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        category = doc.add_item(Category, name=label, label=label)
        code_list.codes.append(
            CodeItem(
                agency=code_list.agency,
                identifier=str(uuid4()),
                version=code_list.version,
                value=str(number),
                category=category.to_reference(),
            )
        )


with open("health-survey.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
columns = list(rows[0])

doc = ddi.new_study(
    title="International Health Survey 2024", agency="health-research.example.org"
)
# RespondentID is assigned, not asked, so it gets no question.
QUESTIONS = {
    "Country": "In which country do you live?",
    "Age": "How old are you?",
    "Sex": "What is your sex?",
    "HeightCm": "How tall are you, in centimetres?",
    "WeightKg": "How much do you weigh, in kilograms?",
    "SmokingStatus": "Which of these best describes your smoking?",
    "ExerciseFrequency": "How often do you exercise for at least 30 minutes?",
    "AlcoholDrinksPerWeek": "How many alcoholic drinks do you have in a typical week?",
    "SelfRatedHealth": "In general, how would you rate your health?",
    "ChronicCondition": "Do you have a long-term health condition?",
    "DoctorVisitsLastYear": "How many times did you see a doctor in the last 12 months?",
    "HasHealthInsurance": "Do you have health insurance?",
    "SleepHours": "On a typical night, how many hours do you sleep?",
    "Wellbeing": "On a scale of 0 to 10, how satisfied are you with your life?",
}
questions = {col: doc.add_question(text=text) for col, text in QUESTIONS.items()}
variables = {
    col: doc.add_variable(name=col, question=questions.get(col)) for col in columns
}

for col in ("SmokingStatus", "ExerciseFrequency"):
    code_list = doc.add_code_list(name=f"{col} Codes")
    add_codes(doc, code_list, sorted({row[col] for row in rows}))
    variables[col].set_coded(code_list)

for name in (
    "Physical Health",
    "Mental Health",
    "Access to Healthcare",
    "Demographics",
):
    doc.add_concept(name=name)
doc.add_universe(name="Adults aged 18 and over in the participating countries")

# Lineage: BMI is computed from height and weight
bmi = doc.add_variable(name="BMI", label="Body mass index")
bmi.source_variable_references = [
    variables["HeightCm"].to_reference(),
    variables["WeightKg"].to_reference(),
]

# Linkage: the register is a second study, joined on RespondentID
register = doc.add_study(title="Hospital Admissions Register 2024")
register_ds = doc.study(register.identifier)
register_key = register_ds.add_variable(name="RespondentID")
admissions = register_ds.add_variable(name="HospitalAdmissions")
variables["RespondentID"].set_property("linkage_role", "key")
register_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")

link = doc.add_comparison(name="Survey-to-register linkage 2024")
exact = link.correspondence(
    commonality="The same respondent identifier in both sources.", weight=1.0
)
link.add_variable_map(
    variables["RespondentID"].to_reference(),
    register_key.to_reference(),
    correspondence=exact,
)
link.set_property("linkage_method", "deterministic")
linked = doc.add_variable(name="HealthByHospitalUse")
linked.source_variable_references = [
    variables["SelfRatedHealth"].to_reference(),
    admissions.to_reference(),
]

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
# -> v1: 0 validation errors, 0 lint errors
doc.save("health-survey-v1.xml")

# Version 1.1
dentist = doc.add_question(
    text="How many times did you see a dentist in the last 12 months?"
)
doc.add_variable(name="DentistVisitsLastYear", question=dentist)
study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[InternationalString(text="Added dental visit frequency question")]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Principal Investigator"
print(f"v1.1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors")
# -> v1.1: 0 validation errors
doc.save("health-survey-v1.1.xml")

Track C: Archivist: Enrich and Version Existing DDI Files: Sample solution

One loop over the three files from step 1.

from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem

ARCHIVE_FIELDS = {
    "archive:accession_date": "Date the archive received the file.",
    "archive:depositor": "Team that deposited the file.",
    "archive:retention": "How long the archive keeps the file.",
    "archive:access": "Who may use the data: open, registered or restricted.",
}
YES_NO_FILES = {3}  # from the plan: study 3 asks a yes/no question


def set_archive_field(item, key, value):
    if key not in ARCHIVE_FIELDS:
        raise KeyError(f"{key!r} is not in the archive catalog")
    item.set_property(key, value)


def count_archive_fields(doc):
    items = [doc.study_unit, *doc.questions, *doc.variables]
    return sum(
        any(key.startswith("archive:") for key in item.properties) for item in items
    )


for i in (1, 2, 3):
    doc = ddi.open_ddi(f"study-{i}.xml")
    if not doc.concepts:
        doc.add_concept(name="Social Sciences")
    if not doc.universes:
        doc.add_universe(name="General population")
    variable, question = doc.variables[0], doc.questions[0]
    if not variable.question_references:
        variable.question_references = [question.to_reference()]
    if i in YES_NO_FILES:
        yes_no = doc.add_code_list(name="Yes/No")
        for value, label in (("1", "Yes"), ("2", "No")):
            category = doc.add_item(Category, name=label, label=label)
            yes_no.codes.append(
                CodeItem(
                    agency=yes_no.agency,
                    identifier=str(uuid4()),
                    version=yes_no.version,
                    value=value,
                    category=category.to_reference(),
                )
            )
        variable.set_coded(yes_no)

    study = doc.study_unit
    set_archive_field(study, "archive:accession_date", "2024-11-04")
    set_archive_field(study, "archive:depositor", f"Research team {i}")
    set_archive_field(study, "archive:retention", "permanent")
    set_archive_field(variable, "archive:access", "open")

    study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
    study.version_rationales.append(
        VersionRationale(
            descriptions=[
                InternationalString(
                    text="Enriched metadata: added concept, universe, question link and archive fields"
                )
            ]
        )
    )
    study.version_responsibility = "Archive Metadata Team"

    lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
    print(
        f"study-{i}: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, "
        f"{len(lint_errors)} lint errors, "
        f"{count_archive_fields(doc)} items with archive fields"
    )
    doc.save(f"study-{i}-enriched.xml")
# -> study-3: 0 validation errors, 0 lint errors, 2 items with archive fields

Track D: NSO Staff: Build a Census Instrument: Sample solution

One complete script, using census-data.csv. Run validate.sh from step 11 after it.

import csv
from pathlib import Path
from uuid import uuid4

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString, VersionRationale
from ddi_l.models.datacollection import (
    IfThenElse,
    Instrument,
    QuestionConstruct,
    Sequence,
)
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category, CodeItem
from ddi_l.spec import equivalent, load_spec


def add_codes(doc, code_list, labels):
    """Add one Category and one Code per label, numbered from 1."""
    for number, label in enumerate(labels, start=1):
        category = doc.add_item(Category, name=label, label=label)
        code_list.codes.append(
            CodeItem(
                agency=code_list.agency,
                identifier=str(uuid4()),
                version=code_list.version,
                value=str(number),
                category=category.to_reference(),
            )
        )


def rationale(text):
    return VersionRationale(descriptions=[InternationalString(text=text)])


with open("census-data.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
columns = list(rows[0])

doc = ddi.new_study(title="National Census 2024", agency="census.example.gov")
# HouseholdID and PersonNumber are assigned, not asked.
QUESTIONS = {
    "Province": "In which province or territory do you live?",
    "Age": "What was your age at your last birthday?",
    "Gender": "What is your gender?",
    "MaritalStatus": "What is your marital status?",
    "RelationshipToHead": "What is your relationship to Person 1?",
    "CountryOfBirth": "In which country were you born?",
    "Citizenship": "Of what country are you a citizen?",
    "MotherTongue": "What language did you first learn at home in childhood?",
    "HighestEducation": "What is the highest level of education you have completed?",
    "EmploymentType": "Last week, were you an employee, self-employed, or not working?",
    "Occupation": "What was your main kind of work last week?",
    "WeeklyHoursWorked": "How many hours did you work last week?",
    "AnnualIncome": "What was your total income last year?",
    "CommuteMode": "How did you usually get to work last week?",
    "HousingType": "What type of dwelling do you live in?",
    "Tenure": "Is this dwelling owned or rented by a member of this household?",
    "Rooms": "How many rooms are in this dwelling?",
    "YearBuilt": "In what year was this dwelling built?",
    "HouseholdSize": "How many people usually live here?",
    "InternetAccess": "Does this household have access to the internet at home?",
}
questions = {col: doc.add_question(text=text) for col, text in QUESTIONS.items()}
variables = {
    col: doc.add_variable(name=col, question=questions.get(col)) for col in columns
}

for col in ("Province", "Gender", "MaritalStatus", "EmploymentType", "HousingType"):
    code_list = doc.add_code_list(name=f"{col}Codes")
    add_codes(doc, code_list, sorted({row[col] for row in rows}))
    variables[col].set_coded(code_list)

doc.add_concept(name="Population")
doc.add_concept(name="Labour")
doc.add_universe(name="All persons usually resident in private dwellings")
variables["Occupation"].set_property("classification", "ISCO-08")
variables["AnnualIncome"].set_property("referencePeriod", "Calendar year 2023")

# The flow: everyone answers the person section; the labour section has a gate
AGE_GATE = "Age >= 15"


def ask(col):
    return doc.add_item(
        QuestionConstruct, name=col, question_reference=questions[col].to_reference()
    )


person = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="person",
    control_construct_references=[ask(c).to_reference() for c in ("Age", "Gender")],
)
labour = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="labour",
    control_construct_references=[
        ask(c).to_reference()
        for c in ("EmploymentType", "Occupation", "WeeklyHoursWorked")
    ],
)
gate = doc.add_item(IfThenElse, name="Working-age gate")
gate.set_condition(AGE_GATE, description="Persons aged 15 and over")
gate.then_construct_reference = labour.to_reference()
main = doc.add_item(
    Sequence,
    name="Census flow",
    control_construct_references=[person.to_reference(), gate.to_reference()],
)
instrument = doc.add_item(Instrument, name="Census 2024 questionnaire")
instrument.control_construct_reference = main.to_reference()

# The spec of the same flow. A person with no age skips the labour section.
Path("census.spec.yaml").write_text(
    """\
spec: census-2024
version: "1"
modules:
  - id: person
    questions:
      - id: Age
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 120, decimals: 0}}
  - id: labour
    gate: Age >= 15
    questions:
      - id: EmploymentType
        domain: {text: {max_length: 40}}
      - id: Occupation
        domain: {text: {max_length: 60}}
      - id: WeeklyHoursWorked
        domain: {numeric: {min: 0, max: 168, decimals: 0}}
""",
    encoding="utf-8",
)
spec = load_spec("census.spec.yaml")
print(f"Gates agree: {equivalent(spec.module('labour').gate_text, AGE_GATE)}")
# -> Gates agree: True

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v1: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
doc.save("census-v1.xml")

# Version 1.1: one question added
q_internet = doc.add_question(text="Do you have access to high-speed internet?")
doc.add_variable(name="HighSpeedInternet", question=q_internet)
study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
study.version_rationales.append(rationale("Added internet access question"))
study.version_responsibility = "Census Content Team"
doc.save("census-v1.1.xml")

# Version 2.0: five questions added, three retired with their variables
for text in [
    "What is your primary language at home?",
    "Do you identify as Indigenous?",
    "What is your highest degree?",
    "Do you have a disability?",
    "What is your annual household income?",
]:
    doc.add_question(text=text)
for col in ("Province", "MaritalStatus", "HousingType"):
    doc.remove(variables[col].identifier)
    doc.remove(questions[col].identifier)
study.increment_major_version()
study.version_rationales = [
    rationale("Major redesign: added equity and income questions")
]

lint_errors = [f for f in doc.lint() if f.severity == "error"]
print(f"v2: {len(doc.validate())} validation errors, {len(lint_errors)} lint errors")
# -> v2: 0 validation errors, 0 lint errors
doc.save("census-v2.xml")

docs.title: Cheat sheet
docs.text: This page is a quick reference for the ddi-l package. Keep it open while you work through the modules or build your own projects.

docs.title: The basics in 30 seconds
docs.text:
import ddi_l as ddi

doc = ddi.new_study(title="My Survey", agency="example.org")
q = doc.add_question(text="How old are you?", label="Age question")
v = doc.add_variable(name="Age", question=q, label="Age in years")
doc.save("my-survey.xml")

That is enough to create a valid DDI document. Everything below adds detail.

label= is optional and worth the few characters: ddi lint reports every maintainable without one, so a document written without labels arrives warning about itself. Pass label_lang= when the label is in a different language from the name.

docs.title: Create, open, and save
docs.text: What you want to do Code Create a new study doc = ddi.new_study(title="...", agency="...") Open an existing file doc = ddi.open_ddi("file.xml") Open with validation doc = ddi.open_ddi("file.xml", validate=True) Save to disk doc.save("file.xml") Validate before saving errors = doc.validate()

docs.title: Add items to a study
docs.text:
# Questions
q = doc.add_question(text="What is your income?")

# Variables (linked to a question)
v = doc.add_variable(name="Income", question=q)

# Concepts
c = doc.add_concept(name="Economic Status")

# Universes
u = doc.add_universe(name="Adults aged 18+")

# Variables with concept and universe
v = doc.add_variable(name="Income", question=q, concept=c)

# Code lists
cl = doc.add_code_list(name="Gender Codes")

docs.title: Variable types (representations)
docs.text:
Say what kind of values a variable holds. Each setter returns the variable, so you can chain it onto add_variable:

doc.add_variable(name="age").set_numeric("Integer", low=0, high=120)
doc.add_variable(name="sex").set_coded(cl)  # values from a code list
doc.add_variable(name="comment").set_text()  # free text
doc.add_variable(name="dob").set_datetime("Date")

docs.title: Count and list items
docs.text:
print(len(doc.questions))  # Number of questions
print(len(doc.variables))  # Number of variables
print(len(doc.concepts))  # Number of concepts
print(len(doc.universes))  # Number of universes
print(len(doc.code_lists))  # Number of code lists

for q in doc.questions:
    print(q.identifier)

docs.title: Find, remove, and add any type
docs.text:
# Find an item by identifier
item = doc.find("my-identifier")

# Remove an item by identifier
doc.remove("my-identifier")

# Add any DDI type (Category, Instrument, etc.)
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category

cat = doc.add_item(Category, name="Male")

# List all items of a type
for cat in doc.items(Category):
    print(cat.identifier)

docs.title: Custom properties
docs.text:
# Set a property
q.set_property("sensitivity", "high")

# Read a property
print(q.get_property("sensitivity"))  # "high"

# List all properties
print(q.properties)  # {"sensitivity": "high"}

# Remove a property
q.remove_property("sensitivity")

docs.title: Custom fields (extend the standard)
docs.text:
DDI is open: add organization-specific fields through the standard's own extension points, and they stay inside valid DDI and round-trip on save.

from ddi_l.models.base import UserID

# Namespace your keys so they never collide with another org's
v.set_property("myorg:retention_policy", "destroy after 7 years")
v.set_property("myorg:source_system", "CRM-2024")

# Back a custom field with a controlled vocabulary (references the code list URN)
quality = doc.add_code_list(name="Quality Flag Codes")  # a code list = the vocabulary
v.set_property("myorg:quality_flag", "validated")  # a value from the vocabulary
v.set_property("myorg:quality_flag_codes", quality)  # references the code list

# An organization-specific external identifier (value + type)
v.user_ids.append(UserID(value="CAT-000734", type_of_user_id="InternalCatalogue"))

# Audit which items carry your custom fields
tagged = [x for x in doc.variables if any(k.startswith("myorg:") for k in x.properties)]

Custom fields serialize to r:UserAttributePair (and r:UserID), which is still valid DDI. See Module 14.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
item = doc.add_variable(name="age")  # or any DDI item

# Read the current version
print(item.version)  # "1": newly created items start at "1"

# Set a three-part version if you want major/minor/patch semantics
item.version = "1.0.0"

# Bump the version
item.increment_major_version()  # 1.0.0 → 2.0.0
item.increment_minor_version()  # 1.0.0 → 1.1.0
item.increment_subversion()  # 1.0.0 → 1.0.1

# Record why you changed something
from ddi_l.models.base import VersionRationale, InternationalString

item.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[InternationalString(text="Added income question for 2024 wave")]
    )
)
item.version_responsibility = "Survey Design Team"

Edit an item that is already in the file, then version it (see Module 15, sections 6 and 7):

question.question_texts[0].text = "In a typical week, do you work from home?"
question.increment_subversion()
variable.set_coded(new_code_list)  # switch to another code list
variable.increment_major_version()

# After a version bump, point references at the new version
variable.question_references = [
    question.to_reference() if ref.identifier == question.identifier else ref
    for ref in variable.question_references
]

docs.title: Questionnaire flow constructs
docs.text:
Questionnaire flow (the order questions are asked, and "skip" or "branch" rules) is built from these control constructs:

Construct What it does QuestionConstruct Wraps one question so it can sit in a flow Sequence Runs steps in order (step 1, step 2, step 3) IfThenElse Branches based on a condition (skip logic) StatementItem Shows a message instead of asking a question Instrument The whole questionnaire; points to the top sequence

You add each one with doc.add_item(...), and link them with .to_reference():

from ddi_l.models.datacollection import (
    QuestionConstruct,
    Sequence,
    IfThenElse,
    StatementItem,
    Instrument,
)

q = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?")

# Wrap a question, then group constructs into an ordered section
qc_age = doc.add_item(
    QuestionConstruct, name="Ask Age", question_reference=q.to_reference()
)
section_a = doc.add_item(
    Sequence, name="Section A", control_construct_references=[qc_age.to_reference()]
)
section_c = doc.add_item(Sequence, name="Section C")

# Branch: run section A if true, section C if false
gate = doc.add_item(IfThenElse, name="Age gate")
gate.then_construct_reference = section_a.to_reference()
gate.else_construct_reference = section_c.to_reference()

# Show a message; tie the whole thing together with an Instrument
doc.add_item(StatementItem, name="Welcome to the survey")
doc.add_item(Instrument, name="Survey Instrument")

Loop works the same way (doc.add_item(Loop, name="...")), with its repeated section set via loop.control_construct_reference. See Module 10 for the full worked example.

docs.title: Data files (physical instances)
docs.text:
A PhysicalInstance describes one real data file: where it lives and how big it is. Add it like any other item; it lives at the study level.

from ddi_l.models.physical import PhysicalInstance

pi = doc.add_item(PhysicalInstance, name="2021 Microdata File")
pi.set_data_file("https://example.org/health-2021.csv")  # where the file is
pi.set_record_count(15000)  # how many records

name becomes the file's citation title (a physical instance has no Name element in DDI).

To say where each variable sits in that file, add a record layout:

rl = doc.add_record_layout()
rl.add_data_item(age.to_reference(), start_position=1, width=2)
rl.add_data_item(income.to_reference(), start_position=3, width=8)

Omit the positions for a delimited (comma/tab) file.

To update many variables from a new data file, and version each change, see Module 15, "Going further".

docs.title: Logical records and cubes
docs.text:
# A logical record = which variables make up one case (one row)
dr = doc.add_data_relationship()
dr.add_logical_record()  # all variables, the usual rectangular file

# An NCube = multidimensional (cube) data: axes + measured values
cube = doc.add_ncube(name="Population by year and region")
cube.add_dimension(year.to_reference())
cube.add_dimension(region.to_reference())
cube.add_measure(population.to_reference())

# Attach an attribute to a specific region of the cube
region = cube.add_coordinate_region()
cube.add_dimension_value(region, rank=1, code_references=[code_2020.to_reference()])
cube.add_attribute(footnote.to_reference(), attachment_region=region)

Fine-grained physical and inline-data forms:

# Numeric range with inclusivity flags and missing values
age.set_numeric(
    "Integer",
    low=0,
    high=120,
    low_inclusive=True,
    high_inclusive=False,
    missing_values=["-9", "-8"],
)

# A data item's storage details in a fixed-width/delimited file
layout.add_data_item(
    age.to_reference(),
    start_position=1,
    width=3,
    storage_format="ASCII",
    delimiter="comma",
    decimal_positions=2,
)

# Inline data as a RecordSet (rows) or VariableSet (columns)
ds = doc.add_dataset(name="Sample rows")
ds.set_variable_order([age.to_reference(), sex.to_reference()])
ds.add_record(["42", "M"])
ds.add_variable_item(age.to_reference(), ["42", "37"])  # column form

# Harmonization: scheme-to-scheme and representation maps
cmp = doc.add_comparison(name="2020 to 2021")
cmp.add_managed_item_map(
    [(age_2020.to_reference(), age_2021.to_reference())], type_of_mapped_item="Variable"
)
cmp.add_representation_map(
    codes_2020.to_reference(), codes_2021.to_reference(), recode.to_reference()
)

docs.title: Organize a study into a group
docs.text:
# Wrap the study in a Group (a study series / publication package)
doc.add_group()
# The document stays editable; this still reaches the grouped study
doc.add_variable(name="region")

# Add more studies to the series, and map items across them
wave2 = doc.add_study(title="Wave 2")
# Edit a specific study via its cursor (doc.study() targets the primary)
doc.study(wave2.identifier).add_variable(name="income")
cmp = doc.add_comparison(name="2020 to 2021")
cmp.add_variable_map(age_2020.to_reference(), age_2021.to_reference())

docs.title: Instance-level packages and translation
docs.text:
# Archive-specific lifecycle metadata for the study
doc.add_archive()

# Reusable metadata shared across studies (a ResourcePackage)
doc.add_resource_package()

# A local holding of a deposited study (references the primary study by default)
doc.add_local_holding_package()

# Record which languages the instance was translated between
doc.add_translation_information(
    languages=["en", "fr"], description="Translated from French."
)

docs.title: Data lineage (variable derivation)
docs.text:
# Collection variable, linked to a question
v_age = doc.add_variable(name="age", question=q_age)

# Derived variable, linked to its source variable(s)
from ddi_l.models.base import Reference

v_age_group = doc.add_variable(name="age_group")
v_age_group.source_variable_references = [
    Reference(agency="health.gc.ca", identifier=v_age.identifier, version="1"),
]

# Multi-source derivation
v_bmi = doc.add_variable(name="bmi")
v_bmi.source_variable_references = [
    Reference(agency="health.gc.ca", identifier=v_height.identifier, version="1"),
    Reference(agency="health.gc.ca", identifier=v_weight.identifier, version="1"),
]

docs.title: Data linkage (combining datasets)
docs.text:
Link records from two sources that share a common variable (the linkage key). Each source is its own study in a group, a Comparison records how the keys correspond, and linked variables trace back to both sources.

import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import Reference

# Source 1: survey (the primary study)
doc = ddi.new_study(title="Survey", agency="statcan.gc.ca")
survey_key = doc.add_variable(name="anon_id")
survey_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")  # tag the common key
survey_health = doc.add_variable(name="health_rating")

# Source 2: admin register (a second study in the group)
admin = doc.add_study(title="Admin register")
admin_ds = doc.study(admin.identifier)
admin_key = admin_ds.add_variable(name="anon_id")
admin_key.set_property("linkage_role", "key")
admin_visits = admin_ds.add_variable(name="hospital_visits")

# Map the keys; record the linkage method and quality
cmp = doc.add_comparison(name="Survey-to-Admin Linkage")
match = cmp.correspondence(commonality="Shared anonymized id.", weight=1.0)
cmp.add_variable_map(
    survey_key.to_reference(), admin_key.to_reference(), correspondence=match
)
cmp.set_property("linkage_method", "deterministic")  # or "probabilistic"
cmp.set_property("match_rate", "0.94")

# Linked variable: provenance to BOTH sources
linked = doc.add_variable(name="health_by_hospital_use")
linked.source_variable_references = [
    Reference(agency="statcan.gc.ca", identifier=survey_health.identifier, version="1"),
    Reference(agency="statcan.gc.ca", identifier=admin_visits.identifier, version="1"),
]

Cross-study source_variable_references warn on save. That is expected for linkage. See Module 12.

docs.title: Multi-language support
docs.text:
from ddi_l.models.base import InternationalString

# Create a question in English (default)
q = doc.add_question(text="What is your age?", lang="en")

# Add a French translation
q.question_texts.append(InternationalString(text="Quel est votre âge ?", lang="fr"))

docs.title: Read data from CSV or Excel
docs.text:
Sample file: survey_sample.csv

import csv
import ddi_l as ddi

# From CSV
with open("survey_sample.csv") as f:
    columns = csv.DictReader(f).fieldnames

# Question wording from the questionnaire; unlisted columns get no question
QUESTIONS = {
    "age": "How old are you?",
    "gender": "What is your gender?",
    "income": "What was your total income last year, before taxes?",
    "education_level": "What is the highest level of education you have completed?",
}

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Survey", agency="example.org")
for col in columns:
    q = doc.add_question(text=QUESTIONS[col]) if col in QUESTIONS else None
    doc.add_variable(name=col, question=q)
doc.save("survey.xml")

# From Excel (requires pandas + openpyxl)
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_excel("survey.xlsx")
for col in df.columns:
    doc.add_variable(name=col)

docs.title: CLI commands
docs.text:
Run these in your terminal.

Command What it does ddi validate file.xml Check a file against the DDI schema ddi lint file.xml Run best-practice checks ddi to-json file.xml Convert DDI XML to JSON ddi from-json file.json -o file.xml Convert JSON back to DDI XML ddi roundtrip in.xml -o out.xml Read and re-write (tests fidelity) ddi versions file.xml Show version info from the file ddi spec validate spec.yaml Check a questionnaire spec (Module 16) ddi conform file.xml --spec spec.yaml Compare an instrument with its spec

Exit code 0 means success. Exit code 1 means failure.

docs.title: Build a complete study from a CSV
docs.text:
import csv
import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.logicalproduct import Category

doc = ddi.new_study(title="Household Survey", agency="stats.example.org")
universe = doc.add_universe(name="All households in Canada")

QUESTIONS = {
    "age": "How old are you?",
    "gender": "What is your gender?",
    "income": "What was your total income last year, before taxes?",
    "education_level": "What is the highest level of education you have completed?",
}

with open("survey_sample.csv") as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    for col in reader.fieldnames:
        q = doc.add_question(text=QUESTIONS[col]) if col in QUESTIONS else None
        concept = doc.add_concept(name=col.replace("_", " ").title())
        doc.add_variable(name=col, question=q, concept=concept)

errors = doc.validate()
if not errors:
    doc.save("household-survey.xml")
    print("Saved and valid.")

docs.title: Open, enrich, version, and re-save
docs.text:
import ddi_l as ddi
from ddi_l.models.base import VersionRationale, InternationalString

doc = ddi.open_ddi("survey-v1.xml")

q = doc.add_question(text="What is your email address?")
doc.add_variable(name="Email", question=q)

study = doc.study_unit
study.increment_minor_version(allow_dotted=True)
study.version_rationales.append(
    VersionRationale(
        descriptions=[InternationalString(text="Added email question for wave 2")]
    )
)
study.version_responsibility = "Survey Team"

doc.validate()
doc.save("survey-v2.xml")

docs.title: Training curriculum
docs.text:
Welcome to the ddi-l training curriculum. This course teaches you how to document surveys, censuses, and datasets using the DDI standard and Python. No prior experience with DDI or XML is needed.

This is the place to learn ddi-l step by step. The user guide is a one-page reference of the same API, and the how-to guides cover single tasks once you know the basics.

What this course covers

You will learn to turn a CSV or Excel file into a fully documented DDI package, complete with questions, variables, concepts, code lists, custom properties, versioning, and validation.

docs.title: How the course is organized
docs.text:
The curriculum has 17 modules in three tiers. Each module lists its prerequisites at the top, and the table below repeats them: most modules need only the one before, but some need more. You check your work from Module 3 onwards, and by the end of Tier 1 you can open, change and validate any DDI file.

The times are the ones each module gives: working alone (self-paced), or in a class with an instructor (instructor-led).

# Module Self-paced Instructor-led Prerequisites Tier 1: Foundations 1 What is metadata? 30 min 45 min None 2 Set up your environment 20 min 30 min Module 1 3 Create your first study 30 min 45 min Module 2 4 Variables and questions 30 min 40 min Module 3 5 Concepts and universes 30 min 40 min Module 4 6 Open and modify files 30 min 40 min Module 5 7 Validate from the command line 30 min 40 min Module 6 Tier 2: Real-world skills 8 From CSV/Excel to DDI 45 min 60 min Module 7 9 Code lists 40 min 50 min Module 8 10 Questionnaire flows 50 min 60 min Module 9 11 Data lineage 60 min 75 min Module 10 12 Data linkage 60 min 75 min Module 11 13 Properties, find, and validate 40 min 50 min Module 12 14 Custom fields 45 min 55 min Module 13 15 Update and version 65 min 75 min Module 14 Tier 3: Applied practice 16 Advanced questionnaire specification 75 min 90 min Modules 7, 10 and 15 17 Capstone projects 60-90 min 90 min All (1-16)

Each module starts with numbered learning objectives (O1, O2, ...): what you can do by the end of it, such as write a script or validate a file. Each exercise and quiz question is tagged with the objectives it practises, for example Exercise 2 (O3). Each module ends with a Check yourself list, one line per objective. Tick each line before you move on; for a line you cannot tick, redo the exercises with that tag.

docs.title: Where do I start?
docs.text:
Pick the row that fits you best.

I am a... Start at I can skim Spend extra time on University student (new to data) Module 1 Nothing Modules 3-5 Researcher (know Python, not DDI) Module 1 Module 2 Modules 1, 4 and 5: what DDI calls things Archivist (know DDI, not Python) Module 1 Module 1 Modules 2-7: the Python you need NSO staff (know both) Module 2 Modules 1 and 3 Modules 8-16 Developer automating DDI checks Module 2 Modules 1, 4 and 5 Modules 3 and 7, then the automation track below

docs.title: Automation track
docs.text:
For teams that add DDI validation to pipelines or build services on ddi-l. Take Modules 2, 3 and 7, then work through these guides in order:

Session Focus Pages Pipeline foundations (45 min) Run and configure validation and lint Validate and lint DDI content, CLI recipes Automation (45 min) Script the CLI, keep reports, fail CI on errors Command-line automation playbook, Schema troubleshooting clinic Reuse and integration (45 min) Share fragments, call ddi-l from other systems Fragment reuse lab, HTTP API, Build tools and applications

Review the performance playbook before planning large batch runs.

docs.title: The big picture
docs.text:
This is the process you will learn:

CSV / Excel / SQL table
        ↓
  Python script (ddi-l)
        ↓
  DDI XML document
        ↓
  Validate & version
        ↓
  Archive or publish

To finish Tier 1 in a workshop, add Modules 6 and 7 to the half-day (1 h 20 min more, 4 h 40 min in all): that is a short day rather than a half-day.
